_about: Hand-written node content for the dungeons of data/dungeons/dungeons.json (the CSV import). Everything here is placeholder-grade text and numbers (balance is out of scope). Per dungeon: defaults (deck archetypes, icons, AIs cycled over its battles), boss (deck/hp/icon), foes (node number -> foe name, or an object {name, deck, size, hp, ai, icon, extra}), events / challenges / loot (node number -> content), blurbs, story_keys (node number -> story key `dungeon.<key>.before/.after`, in the zone story file or in `text` below), scenes (node number -> {before, after} cutscene ids). Event/challenge effects are tokens: heal:N damage:N gold:N pay:N lose:N card:ID boon:Name|max_hp=2,atk=1,def=1,start_hp=1 (curse:Name|max_hp=-1 is the same with negative numbers) rescue sever. An event may be {ref: id} naming one the dungeon class still builds in code.

5.title: Locker Room of Legends
5.body: Rows of lockers hold the old champions' gear, every strap labelled by weight class. A laminated sign reads LOCKER 13 IS A STATE OF MIND. One door hangs ajar, humming the theme from a boxing movie.
choices: It smells of victory, eucalyptus and somebody else's victory. It is also warm. You feel sturdier and very slightly watched.
Protein bars, a roll of gold and a note: 'Spotter knows.' Somewhere a whistle blows. You keep the gold and the shame.
Do a set with the ghost of a champion
He miscounts your reps on purpose, to be encouraging. You leave taller, if not stronger, and he presses a Gym Bro's number into your hand.

12.title: The Sauna of Truth
12.text: The steam asks one honest question: how hard do you lead?

7.title: The Corrupted Pantry
7.body: Shelves of glowing, sickly-green food hum softly. A ladle is still stirring a pot that nobody is minding, and the pot has started to hum back.
choices: It is delicious. It is probably cursed. You feel strong and slightly sticky, and your units will not stop smelling of gravy.
Some of the pantry is still clean. The jars are labelled DO NOT OPEN, WE MEAN IT. You do not open them. You sell them.
It has been stirring for ten years and nobody ever asked it to stop. It sighs, hands you a Sourdough Sentry out of gratitude, and finally rests.

10.title: R&D Archives
10.body: Blueprints, recipe cards and signed memos fill the cabinets. Every handwritten note signed by the Grand Chef leans the wrong way, as if written by someone who has only ever read about left-handedness.
choices: The chef who wrote these has never held a ladle. The impostor is exposed, and so is how little they have been cooking.
Evidence, and a buyer for it. The buyer asks no questions, which is the best kind of buyer.
Pocket the recipe marked DO NOT SERVE
It is one line long and ends with 'send it back.' You can see why it was classified.

4.title: Taste Test Lab
4.text: Beakers, spoons and a very small flag: does your deck have the body for the panel?

blurbs.11: The cannon-blender is fed protein and plates in equal measure. Every Ingredient and every Iron goes into the same shaker, and something six feet tall comes out.

2.title: Take-a-Number Kiosk
2.body: A small grey machine offers you a ticket. The display above says NOW SERVING 3. Your number is 4,000,213. A polite ghost behind you coughs, then apologises for coughing.
choices: You wait. You wait some more. You feel seen, and slightly worse. A vending machine dispenses one sad cookie.
The machine jams, apologises and coughs up coins and a written warning. You are now marked 'Difficult.'
Nobody dares object. Yet. Number 4,000,213 is quietly becoming a legend.

8.title: Form 27-B Office
8.body: Form 27-B requires Form 27-C, which requires a stamp from the office you are standing in. A clerk slides a pen across the counter without looking up.
choices: Everything is in order. A boon is granted and a small tax is levied, in that order, by two different departments.
It works! Mostly. Something in the ceiling disapproves, loudly, with a stapler.
Ask the clerk what Form 27-C is
The clerk looks up for the first time in decades. Nobody has ever asked. She slides you a Pink Slip 'for personal use' and, you swear, winks.

12.title: The Shredding Room
12.body: Rows of paper shredders chew through the day's denied appeals. A sign reads: SHRED ONE THING, RECEIVE ONE THING. Another, in smaller letters, reads: THINGS INCLUDE YOU.
choices: The shredder hums happily and pays out in coins. It says 'denied' in a voice like a kettle.
Nothing is left of Number 4,000,213. You feel lighter, and slightly nonexistent. The machine files you under 'Resolved.'
Reach in for what it ate
You pull out half of a lost appeal. It is, technically, a weapon. The machine takes a bite of you in exchange.

5.title: Waiting Room of Eternity
5.text: Row after row of chairs. Can your deck outwait the line?

blurbs.13: The elevator is hand-cranked by a Beefcake on loan from the wheels. Every floor needs a permit and a rep. Iron turns the crank; Red Tape keeps the doors shut.

7.title: Weeping Compost Pool
7.body: The pool is the colour of a bruise and it is sobbing very quietly. Things float in it that used to be useful. A boot, mostly.
choices: It tastes of rain and regret. You feel hardier, and a little poisoned.
Somebody will pay for this. Somebody always does. It is usually a hedgehog.
You tell it that it is doing great. It sobs harder, then gives you a very old Mulch Mole it was keeping safe, and a bit of its warmth.

12.title: The Heart Roots
12.body: Thick, pulsing roots run from every wall into the chamber beyond: the Rotheart's lifelines. You could cut them. It will hurt, her more than you.
choices: The roots shriek and let go. Whatever waits ahead will be weaker for it.
The roots keep pulsing. The Rotheart keeps its strength.

4.title: Strangled Greenhouse
4.text: The vines are choosing who gets through. Can your deck keep its footing?

blurbs.10: The mutant bees have learned farming. What the rot throws away they turn into honey, and what they make they feed back to the rot.
blurbs.11: Something lifts in the Rot Tunnel. Every scrap of Garbage it finds becomes a rep, and every rep becomes Iron.

14.name: Percival Plume, Deputy Minister of Good News

3.title: Grand Foyer
3.body: A portrait of a smiling ruler fills the wall. The floor is so polished you can see yourself, and he is standing behind you in every reflection.
choices: The smile never changes. Neither, you realise, does anything else here. It is strangely restful.
Heavier than it looks, worth more than it should be, and covered in your fingerprints in a building that remembers fingerprints.
There is always one more than there should be. You wave. He waves second. You are, for a moment, a little less afraid of him.

12.title: The Doppelganger's Lab Notes
12.body: A lab table of food notes: a shapeshifter's recipe for becoming a Grand Chef, with an entire page on how to smile like her. The margins are full of practice smiles.
choices: It explains everything, including why the sauce tastes of nothing. There is no Grand Chef in here, only a very good understudy.
Somebody downstairs will pay for them. Nobody upstairs will miss them. That is the whole plan.
Practise the smile in the mirror
It is perfect. It is horrifying. Your face stays like that for a while, and the guards leave you alone.

22.title: Garden of Uniform Flowers
22.body: A thousand identical flowers stand in identical rows. You count them twice. One of them is, very slightly, a different shade of yellow.
choices: It tastes of dandelion. It feels like the first honest thing in the castle.
Pick a handful of the rest
They wilt in your hand and leave behind a few coins, which is more than they should have been able to do.
You press a bent stem into the soil. The gardener will find it tomorrow and have to rethink everything. You walk on, lighter.

S-IRON._note: Gainlands v2, Part F: the Iron Cave, tuned for the start of the game (small decks, low HP).

blurbs.2: The conveyor never stops, like the Eternal Queue it was modelled on. Each plate comes with a numbered ticket, stamped.
The Courtier collects the crusts the kingdom leaves behind and serves them back, warmed, as a royal tasting menu.
The junction crew trains on scrap: tyre flips, bin presses, dumbbells made of drain pipe. Every Garbage becomes muscle.

3.name: Colonel Cornelius Crumb, Director of Culinary Defense

blurbs.1: A queue of grey citizens, a grey ladle, a supervisor timing every scoop.
blurbs.2: Vats the size of houses. Something in the third one is humming the national anthem.
blurbs.3: Behind a ration hatch: a real kitchen, a locked pantry and a badger in medals.

4.title: The Observation Deck
4.body: A gallery of glass above the cells, a kettle, a cracked mug that says WORLD'S OKAYEST PATH-OLOGIST, and a corkboard of notes on one subject. The newest are a count of days.
choices: Read the notes on the Subject
Drain cycles, power readings, a column labelled 'cooperative?' that someone has filled in with 'asks for his mother.' You put the notes down very carefully.
It is the first thing here that tastes like anything. You feel steadier.
Keycards, a petty cash tin, and a half-written resignation letter.

7.title: The Draining Chamber
7.body: A round chamber, glass on every side, a chair at the center with straps worn pale. Cables run from the chair to four great tanks, each glowing a different color. This is where it was done.
choices: Put your hand on the glass
The four colors lean toward your palm like plants toward a window. They were yours. They remember.
Every cycle logged, every reading neat. You learn exactly how the machine works, which is how to break it.
They come away easily. They were only ever as strong as the people who buckled them.

12.title: The Mentor's Study
12.body: A warm, cluttered study with the only rug in the Lab. On the desk lies an open journal in a neat, slanted hand.
choices: Take the journal for Wren's true record
It goes into your pack, light as a confession.
Let him find it open. Let him wonder who read it.

6.title: Decontamination
6.text: Four nozzles hiss in four colors. A sensor asks whether your deck can carry more than one Path at a time.

quest.meet_the_merchants.active: Sable, Tilly and Pip, dearie, all on the square. And buy a card from Sable. You are not leaving this town with only what a cave gave you.
quest.meet_the_merchants.ready: Back already. Sable charmed you, Tilly was a colour, Pip measured you. That is {town}, dearie. Try leaving with the same hat.
Here: a trophy. Everybody gets one. I made it myself, so participate carefully.
quest.first_deck_edit.offer: Now that deck of yours. A deck you never chose is a deck you will lose with.
New cards first. Open a pack: the Menu, top right, then Packs. Or press P, if you are the sort who presses things.
Then the Deck Station, down Champions' Road south of the square. Swap what you like, save it to a slot, and come and tell me.
quest.first_deck_edit.offer_pack: No packs at all? Here, dearie. A General Pack. Slightly sat on. Cards are cards.
quest.first_deck_edit.active_pack: Open the pack first, dearie. Menu, then Packs. It will not open itself. I have asked.
quest.first_deck_edit.active: The Deck Station, dearie. Champions' Road, south of the square. Save it to a slot, or it doesn't count. I check.
quest.first_deck_edit.ready: Sorted and saved. Your own deck, at last. Now you may take personal offence when it loses.
quest.storeroom_ghosts.offer: Now, a favour. Tilly's store room, the corner house beside her shop, has been moaning for a week. Not Tilly. The room.
Ghosts, I expect. Petty ones: the worst kind. Nobody can get in for so much as a candle. Go and sort them out. Gently, if they let you.
quest.storeroom_ghosts.active: The store room door, beside Tilly's shop on the north side of the square. Ignore the rattling. That is just them being dramatic.
quest.storeroom_ghosts.ready: A refund. Ninety years of haunting, over a refund. I have had customers like that. I still have one.
Well done, dearie. You settled the ghosts. Next, settle yourself somewhere dry.
quest.some_assembly_required.offer: Right. Time you had something sharper than a deck. Bertram Beetsworth issues gear, at the smithy on the west side of the square.
He is... thorough. Report to him, do what he asks, and do not touch his drawer.
quest.some_assembly_required.active: Bertram's smithy, west side of the square. Win him a fight, any fight, and he will stamp something. He lives to stamp something.
quest.path_direction: Armed, are we. Good. Now, where to point you. Start with {zone}, dearie. It is {path} country, and so are you.
{vendor} sells more {path} cards there than anyone in this town. Take gold. Take a bag. Take my advice, for once.
And inside {zone}, your Path stands taller. {buff}: {buff_text}
The Paths quarrel, dearie. Beefcake against Necrocrat, Gourmand against Refusemancer. Since before the roads. Possibly because of them.
So in {zone} the {rival} side gets the short end. {debuff}: {debuff_text} In {rival_zone}, it is your turn to suffer.
{gatekeeper} holds the way in. Win that fight first. Then come back alive. Pie is not cheap.
quest.side_s_town.offer: There is a door under the old well that has been locked since before I was born.
I always thought the key was lost. It was not, dearie. Somebody hid it in a chest in this very town. Find it, and we will see what the door is for.
quest.side_s_town.active: The key is in a hidden chest in town. Look in the odd corners, dearie. This town has never quite managed a straight one.
quest.side_s_town.ready: You found it. Look at the bow: four little carvings, in a ring. Hm. Never mind. I am too old for stairs, dearie. You are not.
quest.side_s_town.done: The iron hatch beside the well. Go on. Whatever is under it belonged to the Old Kingdom, not to me. Mind the stairs.
quest.side_s_beef.offer: Only the worthy reach the top. Also bring water.

There's a mountain behind the station... and a barbell on top older than the regime. Older than me, nearly. Bring me a protein shake from the stand and I'll show you the way. Can't climb on an empty cup.
quest.side_s_beef.active: Water, friend. A protein shake from the stand will do. Don't spill it. I spilled one, the Festival year... where was I.
quest.side_s_beef.ready: That's the best water I've ever seen. Thank you. Rule one: never lift alone. Rule two... rule two was water.
quest.side_s_beef.done: Mount Swolympus is open. Take the trail behind the station. Mind the thin air... never gets enough credit for being there.
quest.side_s_gour.offer: Over here. Quietly. Have you ever eaten somewhere with no menu? ...I'm brave. I'm brave.
There's a golden reservation card hidden in one of the Buffet's stashes: 'Seating: 1. Courses: 3. Survival: optional.' Find it and I'll tell you where to sit.
quest.side_s_gour.active: The card is in one of the hidden stashes around the Buffet. Golden. You'll know it. Chef always said gold means sit down.
quest.side_s_gour.ready: That's it! One seat, three courses, survival optional. I'm excited. I think. It feels a lot like the other thing.
quest.side_s_gour.done: The sliding door to Omakase is open. Leave your fate to the chef. (quietly) Yes, Chef.
quest.side_s_necro.offer: Number 4,000,212? That's me. They're on 3. Can you help?
The queue in the Waiting Room of Eternity is stuck. Process two of the roaming staff on the D.N.A. floors and I'll get you in. I've brought a book. Several.
quest.side_s_necro.active: Process two roaming staff on the D.N.A. floors. The queue will not move itself. I've given it a very fair chance.
quest.side_s_necro.ready: Two fewer. The queue moved! Slightly. I felt it in my ticket.
quest.side_s_necro.done: The Waiting Room of Eternity will see you now. Take a number. Please leave mine; we've been through so much together.
quest.side_s_ref.offer: SOMEBODY has been eating ALL the compost. Little paw prints. A tiny crown.
Chase off two of the scavengers in the Dump and the trail will lead you to the alley under the big dumpster. Gently, please. They're only hungry. And GUILTY.
quest.side_s_ref.active: Two scavengers in the Dump. Fresh paw prints, freshly stolen compost. A trail of evidence with TERRIBLE table manners.
quest.side_s_ref.ready: The paw prints lead to the big dumpster. I knew it. I KNEW it.
quest.side_s_ref.done: Under the tipped-over dumpster there's a gate made from a bicycle wheel. That's the way to the Trash Panda Throne. Bring a peg for your nose.
npc.kestrel.intro: Psst. Down. The enforcers walk this road on the hour, and they hate surprises. I'm a surprise.
Kestrel. I scout for the Wrinkles. Going into the city? There's an older way in than the gate. Follow the chalk, not the guards. The guards are worse at drawing.
npc.kestrel.return: Road's clear for ten minutes. Chalk's fresh. Move while the guards are busy being punctual somewhere else.
quest.side_s_cap.offer: There's an older way into the city. Nobody remembers it. That's the point.
Get yourself inside and find Wren in the Crease. She'll tell you what the old tunnels are for. Then I'll show you the hatch. Deal?
quest.side_s_cap.active: Get inside and find the Crease: the manhole near the gate. Knock three times. Not two. Two is rude. Then ask Wren about the tunnels.
quest.side_s_cap.ready: You found them. Told you I'd be here. Didn't say where. That's the fun part. Here, you've earned this.
fx.old_tunnels_way_in: The grate beneath the plaza lifts with a groan. Light from the perfect city pours in, and behind you the old tunnels run on: four Paths' services, still connected.
You climb up past the walls. Nobody is watching this way in. Nobody remembers it. That is the point.
quest.side_s_cap.done: The hatch in the north-east of the Outskirts, under the wall, goes down to the Old Service Tunnels. Mind the patrols. And mind my chalk.
dungeon.dg_s_iron_boss.before: On a throne that is really a leg press, a Beefcake with thighs like mill wheels pushes a sled of plates up and down, up and down. He has not stood up in years.
'Nobody. Skips. Leg day.' He presses another rep. 'In my cave. Show me yours. No standing ovation required.'
dungeon.dg_s_iron_boss.after: Baron Quadzilla racks the plates, stands, and wobbles. 'Huh,' he says. 'Standing. Wobbly. Like a first rep.'
He hands you a sweaty ribbon. 'Leg day survivor. Wear it. Stretch. That order.'
dungeon.dg_s_beef_boss.before: A stone colossus sits at the summit with its hands out, palms up, waiting for a barbell. It has been spotting for a thousand years. It is very, very ready.
'Lift,' it rumbles. 'I will catch it. I have always caught it.'
dungeon.dg_s_beef_boss.after: The Ancient Spotter lowers its hands and, for the first time in a thousand years, sets something down. The barbell on the altar is yours.
'One more rep,' it says. Then, quieter: '...That was the one. Thank you for coming up.'
dungeon.dg_s_gour_boss.before: The Itamae Supreme lifts a long knife and does not look up. 'Omakase.'
Behind him, a bull made of toro lowers its horns, politely.
dungeon.dg_s_gour_boss.after: The Itamae bows, wipes his knife on a cloth and slides a small plate across the counter. 'Omakase,' he says. This time it sounds like thank you.
dungeon.dg_s_necro_boss.before: A single desk under a single green lamp, buried in forms. Betty Bones looks up through cat-eye glasses, very slowly, and sighs the sigh of the long deceased.
'Forms A through F,' she says. 'Then we'll talk. We won't, but still.'
dungeon.dg_s_necro_boss.after: Betty stamps one last form with a bony flourish. 'Fine. Number 4,000,212 is approved. Don't make it a thing.'
Far down the line, a ghost with a crumpled ticket begins, very quietly, to cheer.
dungeon.dg_s_ref_boss.before: The Throne of Lids creaks. On it sits a very large raccoon in a very small crown, sweating profusely.
'WE DID NOT EAT THE COMPOST. We sampled it.' His Majesty grips the throne. 'The royal tasting is not open to questions.'
dungeon.dg_s_ref_boss.after: His Majesty abdicates with great dignity and a crust of pizza. The crown rolls under the throne.
'Compost is for the kingdom,' he says. 'We are the kingdom. We fail to see the problem. Do not point at the crumbs.'
dungeon.dg_s_cap_boss.before: A grate lets in light from a perfect city. Beneath it stands Captain Spotless, polishing his shield with a sleeve he has already polished.
'HALT. These tunnels do not exist. You are standing in nothing. I cannot allow you to have found it.'
dungeon.dg_s_cap_boss.after: The Captain sits down on a barrel and, for a moment, looks very tired. 'I remember when these tunnels were full of people,' he says.
'All four Paths, shoulder to shoulder, and nobody measuring anybody. Go on. The grate is not locked.'
dungeon.dg_s_town_boss.before: A four-coloured core hums at the heart of the vault, four marks set in a ring. Beside it a clockwork guardian unfolds, with a sound like a very old clock remembering the hour.
'Tick. Identify,' it says. 'The Old Kingdom's banner is not for just anyone.'
dungeon.dg_s_town_boss.after: The Automaton clicks, whirs and lowers one knee. In its outstretched hand, folded neatly, is the Old Kingdom's banner.
'Tick. ...Recognised. Four Paths. One kingdom. Carry it well.'
quest.cap_paste_works.offer: The dispenser is spoiled. Lovely. But the paste comes from somewhere.
The shuttered stall at the south-west corner hums at night. Stalls are not supposed to hum. Open its ration hatch and look. Gently.
quest.cap_paste_works.active: The south-west stall, the one with its shutter down. Open the ration hatch. Whatever is down there, it will be very, very grey.
quest.cap_paste_works.ready: You shut the vats down? All of them? Then tonight the whole quarter eats something that tastes of something.
Some taste. 'Some' is the best amount.
quest.cap_paste_works.done: I have kept one real onion in my apron for ten years. Tonight, I chop it. You may want to stand back. I will be weeping, and not only from the onion.
event.lab_cell4.title: Cell 4
event.lab_cell4.body: Your old cell: ten years of tally marks, a child's drawing in four colors, and Elowen under it with her hands bound.
event.lab_cell4.result.0: The lock gives. She stands, rubs her wrists and looks at the drawing on the wall for a long moment before she looks at you.
dungeon.lab_cell4.title: Cell 4
